previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease was admitted with severe joint pain in her knees, hips, and right shoulder, consistent with a vaso-occlusive crisis triggered by work-related stress. She was managed with IV hydration, IV and oral hydromorphone for pain, and supplemental oxygen. Laboratory results showed hemolytic anemia with low hemoglobin, low haptoglobin, and elevated reticulocytes. A chest X-ray revealed pulmonary vascular congestion and pleural effusions, prompting concern for high-output heart failure, but echocardiography confirmed normal heart function. Vitamin B12 was initiated due to borderline deficiency. She refused transfusion and improved with supportive care. Pain was successfully tapered to oral medication, and she was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up plans.
